audit_status.source_base: Greek Gospel text tradition, draft aligned to public-domain comparison layer later
audit_status.review_note: Compact complete draft reviewed for empty tomb, Mary Magdalene, beloved disciple, Rabbouni, not-yet-ascended saying, peace/breath/Spirit, Thomas, signs purpose statement.

verses.restored: On the first day of the week, Mary Magdalene comes early, while it is still dark, to the tomb, and sees the stone taken away from the tomb.

familiar.text: The first day of the week cometh Mary Magdalene early, when it was yet dark, unto the sepulchre, and seeth the stone taken away from the sepulchre.

modern.text: Early on the first day of the week, while it was still dark, Mary Magdalene went to the tomb and saw that the stone had been removed from the entrance.

original.text: Τῇ δὲ μιᾷ τῶν σαββάτων Μαρία ἡ Μαγδαληνὴ ἔρχεται πρωῒ σκοτίας ἔτι οὔσης εἰς τὸ μνημεῖον, καὶ βλέπει τὸν λίθον ἠρμένον ἐκ τοῦ μνημείου.

verses.restored: She therefore runs and comes to Simon Peter and to the other disciple whom Jesus loved, and says to them, They have taken the Lord out of the tomb, and we do not know where they laid him.

familiar.text: Then she runneth, and cometh to Simon Peter, and to the other disciple, whom Jesus loved, and saith unto them, They have taken away the LORD out of the sepulchre, and we know not where they have laid him.

modern.text: So she came running to Simon Peter and the other disciple, the one whom Jesus loved. “They have taken the Lord out of the tomb,” she said, “and we do not know where they have put Him!”

original.text: τρέχει οὖν καὶ ἔρχεται πρὸς Σίμωνα Πέτρον καὶ πρὸς τὸν ἄλλον μαθητὴν ὃν ἐφίλει ὁ Ἰησοῦς, καὶ λέγει αὐτοῖς· Ἦραν τὸν κύριον ἐκ τοῦ μνημείου, καὶ οὐκ οἴδαμεν ποῦ ἔθηκαν αὐτόν.

verses.restored: Peter therefore went out, and the other disciple, and they were going to the tomb.

familiar.text: Peter therefore went forth, and that other disciple, and came to the sepulchre.

modern.text: Then Peter and the other disciple set out for the tomb.

original.text: ἐξῆλθεν οὖν ὁ Πέτρος καὶ ὁ ἄλλος μαθητής, καὶ ἤρχοντο εἰς τὸ μνημεῖον.

verses.restored: The two were running together, and the other disciple ran ahead faster than Peter and came first to the tomb.

familiar.text: So they ran both together: and the other disciple did outrun Peter, and came first to the sepulchre.

modern.text: The two were running together, but the other disciple outran Peter and reached the tomb first.

original.text: ἔτρεχον δὲ οἱ δύο ὁμοῦ· καὶ ὁ ἄλλος μαθητὴς προέδραμεν τάχιον τοῦ Πέτρου καὶ ἦλθεν πρῶτος εἰς τὸ μνημεῖον,

verses.restored: Stooping to look, he sees the linen cloths lying there, yet he did not enter.

familiar.text: And he stooping down, and looking in, saw the linen clothes lying; yet went he not in.

modern.text: He bent down and looked in at the linen cloths lying there, but he did not go in.

original.text: καὶ παρακύψας βλέπει κείμενα τὰ ὀθόνια, οὐ μέντοι εἰσῆλθεν.

verses.restored: Simon Peter therefore also comes following him and entered into the tomb; he beholds the linen cloths lying there,

familiar.text: Then cometh Simon Peter following him, and went into the sepulchre, and seeth the linen clothes lie,

modern.text: Simon Peter arrived just after him. He entered the tomb and saw the linen cloths lying there.

original.text: ἔρχεται οὖν ⸀καὶ Σίμων Πέτρος ἀκολουθῶν αὐτῷ, καὶ εἰσῆλθεν εἰς τὸ μνημεῖον· καὶ θεωρεῖ τὰ ὀθόνια κείμενα,

verses.restored: and the face cloth that had been on his head, not lying with the linen cloths but folded up in a place by itself.

familiar.text: And the napkin, that was about his head, not lying with the linen clothes, but wrapped together in a place by itself.

modern.text: The cloth that had been around Jesus’ head was rolled up, lying separate from the linen cloths.

original.text: καὶ τὸ σουδάριον, ὃ ἦν ἐπὶ τῆς κεφαλῆς αὐτοῦ, οὐ μετὰ τῶν ὀθονίων κείμενον ἀλλὰ χωρὶς ἐντετυλιγμένον εἰς ἕνα τόπον·

verses.restored: Then therefore the other disciple, the one having come first to the tomb, also entered; and he saw and trusted.

familiar.text: Then went in also that other disciple, which came first to the sepulchre, and he saw, and believed.

modern.text: Then the other disciple, who had reached the tomb first, also went in. And he saw and believed.

original.text: τότε οὖν εἰσῆλθεν καὶ ὁ ἄλλος μαθητὴς ὁ ἐλθὼν πρῶτος εἰς τὸ μνημεῖον, καὶ εἶδεν καὶ ἐπίστευσεν·

verses.restored: For they did not yet know the Scripture, that it was necessary for him to rise from the dead.

familiar.text: For as yet they knew not the scripture, that he must rise again from the dead.

modern.text: For they still did not understand from the Scripture that Jesus had to rise from the dead. Jesus Appears to Mary Magdalene (Mark 16:9–11)

original.text: οὐδέπω γὰρ ᾔδεισαν τὴν γραφὴν ὅτι δεῖ αὐτὸν ἐκ νεκρῶν ἀναστῆναι.

verses.restored: The disciples therefore went away again to their own.

familiar.text: Then the disciples went away again unto their own home.

modern.text: Then the disciples returned to their homes.

original.text: ἀπῆλθον οὖν πάλιν πρὸς ⸀αὑτοὺς οἱ μαθηταί.

verses.restored: But Mary stood outside by the tomb weeping. As she was weeping, she stooped to look into the tomb.

familiar.text: But Mary stood without at the sepulchre weeping: and as she wept, she stooped down, and looked into the sepulchre,

modern.text: But Mary stood outside the tomb weeping. And as she wept, she bent down to look into the tomb,

original.text: Μαρία δὲ εἱστήκει πρὸς ⸂τῷ μνημείῳ ἔξω κλαίουσα⸃. ὡς οὖν ἔκλαιεν παρέκυψεν εἰς τὸ μνημεῖον,

verses.restored: She beholds two messengers in white sitting, one at the head and one at the feet, where the body of Jesus had lain.

familiar.text: And seeth two angels in white sitting, the one at the head, and the other at the feet, where the body of Jesus had lain.

modern.text: and she saw two angels in white sitting where the body of Jesus had lain, one at the head and the other at the feet.

original.text: καὶ θεωρεῖ δύο ἀγγέλους ἐν λευκοῖς καθεζομένους, ἕνα πρὸς τῇ κεφαλῇ καὶ ἕνα πρὸς τοῖς ποσίν, ὅπου ἔκειτο τὸ σῶμα τοῦ Ἰησοῦ.

verses.restored: They say to her, Woman, why are you weeping? She says to them, They have taken my Lord, and I do not know where they laid him.

familiar.text: And they say unto her, Woman, why weepest thou? She saith unto them, Because they have taken away my LORD, and I know not where they have laid him.

modern.text: “Woman, why are you weeping?” they asked. “Because they have taken my Lord away,” she said, “and I do not know where they have put Him.”

original.text: καὶ λέγουσιν αὐτῇ ἐκεῖνοι· Γύναι, τί κλαίεις; λέγει αὐτοῖς ὅτι Ἦραν τὸν κύριόν μου, καὶ οὐκ οἶδα ποῦ ἔθηκαν αὐτόν.

verses.restored: Saying these things, she turned backward and beholds Jesus standing, and did not know that it was Jesus.

familiar.text: And when she had thus said, she turned herself back, and saw Jesus standing, and knew not that it was Jesus.

modern.text: When she had said this, she turned around and saw Jesus standing there; but she did not recognize that it was Jesus.

original.text: ⸀ταῦτα εἰποῦσα ἐστράφη εἰς τὰ ὀπίσω, καὶ θεωρεῖ τὸν Ἰησοῦν ἑστῶτα, καὶ οὐκ ᾔδει ὅτι Ἰησοῦς ἐστιν.

verses.restored: Jesus says to her, Woman, why are you weeping? Whom do you seek? Thinking that he is the gardener, she says to him, Lord, if you carried him away, tell me where you laid him, and I will take him.

familiar.text: Jesus saith unto her, Woman, why weepest thou? whom seekest thou? She, supposing him to be the gardener, saith unto him, Sir, if thou have borne him hence, tell me where thou hast laid him, and I will take him away.

modern.text: “Woman, why are you weeping?” Jesus asked. “Whom are you seeking?” Thinking He was the gardener, she said, “Sir, if you have carried Him off, tell me where you have put Him, and I will get Him.”

original.text: λέγει ⸀αὐτῇ Ἰησοῦς· Γύναι, τί κλαίεις; τίνα ζητεῖς; ἐκείνη δοκοῦσα ὅτι ὁ κηπουρός ἐστιν λέγει αὐτῷ· Κύριε, εἰ σὺ ἐβάστασας αὐτόν, εἰπέ μοι ποῦ ἔθηκας αὐτόν, κἀγὼ αὐτὸν ἀρῶ.

verses.restored: Jesus says to her, Mary. Turning, she says to him in Hebrew, Rabbouni, which means Teacher.

familiar.text: Jesus saith unto her, Mary. She turned herself, and saith unto him, Rabboni; which is to say, Master.

modern.text: Jesus said to her, “Mary.” She turned and said to Him in Hebrew, “Rabboni!” (which means “Teacher”).

original.text: λέγει ⸀αὐτῇ Ἰησοῦς· ⸀Μαριάμ. στραφεῖσα ἐκείνη λέγει αὐτῷ ⸀Ἑβραϊστί· Ραββουνι (ὃ λέγεται Διδάσκαλε).

verses.restored: Jesus says to her, Do not hold on to me, for I have not yet ascended to the Father. But go to my brothers and say to them, I ascend to my Father and your Father, and my Divine and your Divine.

familiar.text: Jesus saith unto her, Touch me not; for I am not yet ascended to my Father: but go to my brethren, and say unto them, I ascend unto my Father, and your Father; and to my God, and your God.

modern.text: “Do not cling to Me,” Jesus said, “for I have not yet ascended to the Father. But go and tell My brothers, ‘I am ascending to My Father and your Father, to My God and your God.’”

original.text: λέγει ⸀αὐτῇ Ἰησοῦς· Μή μου ἅπτου, οὔπω γὰρ ἀναβέβηκα πρὸς τὸν ⸀πατέρα· πορεύου δὲ πρὸς τοὺς ἀδελφούς μου καὶ εἰπὲ αὐτοῖς· Ἀναβαίνω πρὸς τὸν πατέρα μου καὶ πατέρα ὑμῶν καὶ θεόν μου καὶ θεὸν ὑμῶν.

verses.restored: Mary Magdalene comes announcing to the disciples, I have seen the Lord, and that he said these things to her.

familiar.text: Mary Magdalene came and told the disciples that she had seen the LORD, and that he had spoken these things unto her.

modern.text: Mary Magdalene went and announced to the disciples, “I have seen the Lord!” And she told them what He had said to her. Jesus Appears to the Disciples (Luke 24:36–49; 1 John 1:1–4)

original.text: ἔρχεται ⸀Μαριὰμ ἡ Μαγδαληνὴ ⸀ἀγγέλλουσα τοῖς μαθηταῖς ὅτι ⸀Ἑώρακα τὸν κύριον καὶ ταῦτα εἶπεν αὐτῇ.

verses.restored: When therefore it was evening on that day, the first day of the week, and the doors had been locked where the disciples were because of fear of the Judeans, Jesus came and stood into the midst and says to them, Peace to you.

familiar.text: Then the same day at evening, being the first day of the week, when the doors were shut where the disciples were assembled for fear of the Jews, came Jesus and stood in the midst, and saith unto them, Peace be unto you.

modern.text: It was the first day of the week, and that very evening, while the disciples were together with the doors locked for fear of the Jews, Jesus came and stood among them. “Peace be with you!” He said to them.

original.text: Οὔσης οὖν ὀψίας τῇ ἡμέρᾳ ἐκείνῃ τῇ ⸀μιᾷ σαββάτων, καὶ τῶν θυρῶν κεκλεισμένων ὅπου ἦσαν οἱ ⸀μαθηταὶ διὰ τὸν φόβον τῶν Ἰουδαίων, ἦλθεν ὁ Ἰησοῦς καὶ ἔστη εἰς τὸ μέσον, καὶ λέγει αὐτοῖς· Εἰρήνη ὑμῖν.

verses.restored: Saying this, he showed them the hands and the side. Therefore the disciples rejoiced, seeing the Lord.

familiar.text: And when he had so said, he shewed unto them his hands and his side. Then were the disciples glad, when they saw the LORD.

modern.text: After He had said this, He showed them His hands and His side. The disciples rejoiced when they saw the Lord.

original.text: καὶ τοῦτο εἰπὼν ⸀ἔδειξεν τὰς χεῖρας καὶ τὴν πλευρὰν ⸀αὐτοῖς. ἐχάρησαν οὖν οἱ μαθηταὶ ἰδόντες τὸν κύριον.

verses.restored: Jesus therefore said to them again, Peace to you. Just as the Father has sent me, I also send you.

familiar.text: Then said Jesus to them again, Peace be unto you: as my Father hath sent me, even so send I you.

modern.text: Again Jesus said to them, “Peace be with you. As the Father has sent Me, so also I am sending you.”

original.text: εἶπεν οὖν αὐτοῖς ⸂ὁ Ἰησοῦς⸃ πάλιν· Εἰρήνη ὑμῖν· καθὼς ἀπέσταλκέν με ὁ πατήρ, κἀγὼ πέμπω ὑμᾶς.

verses.restored: Saying this, he breathed into them and says to them, Receive holy Spirit.

familiar.text: And when he had said this, he breathed on them, and saith unto them, Receive ye the Holy Ghost:

modern.text: When He had said this, He breathed on them and said, “Receive the Holy Spirit.

original.text: καὶ τοῦτο εἰπὼν ἐνεφύσησεν καὶ λέγει αὐτοῖς· Λάβετε πνεῦμα ἅγιον·

verses.restored: If you release the sins/misalignments of any, they have been released; if you hold them, they have been held.

familiar.text: Whose soever sins ye remit, they are remitted unto them; and whose soever sins ye retain, they are retained.

modern.text: If you forgive anyone his sins, they are forgiven; if you withhold forgiveness from anyone, it is withheld.” Jesus Appears to Thomas

original.text: ἄν τινων ἀφῆτε τὰς ἁμαρτίας ⸀ἀφέωνται αὐτοῖς· ἄν τινων κρατῆτε κεκράτηνται.

verses.restored: But Thomas, one of the twelve, called Twin, was not with them when Jesus came.

familiar.text: But Thomas, one of the twelve, called Didymus, was not with them when Jesus came.

modern.text: Now Thomas called Didymus, one of the Twelve, was not with the disciples when Jesus came.

original.text: Θωμᾶς δὲ εἷς ἐκ τῶν δώδεκα, ὁ λεγόμενος Δίδυμος, οὐκ ἦν μετʼ αὐτῶν ὅτε ⸀ἦλθεν Ἰησοῦς.

verses.restored: The other disciples therefore were saying to him, We have seen the Lord. But he said to them, Unless I see in his hands the mark of the nails, and put my finger into the mark of the nails and put my hand into his side, I will certainly not trust.

familiar.text: The other disciples therefore said unto him, We have seen the LORD. But he said unto them, Except I shall see in his hands the print of the nails, and put my finger into the print of the nails, and thrust my hand into his side, I will not believe.

modern.text: So the other disciples told him, “We have seen the Lord!” But he replied, “Unless I see the nail marks in His hands, and put my finger where the nails have been, and put my hand into His side, I will never believe.”

original.text: ἔλεγον οὖν αὐτῷ οἱ ἄλλοι μαθηταί· Ἑωράκαμεν τὸν κύριον. ὁ δὲ εἶπεν αὐτοῖς· Ἐὰν μὴ ἴδω ἐν ταῖς χερσὶν αὐτοῦ τὸν τύπον τῶν ἥλων καὶ βάλω τὸν δάκτυλόν μου εἰς τὸν τύπον τῶν ἥλων καὶ βάλω ⸂μου τὴν χεῖρα⸃ εἰς τὴν πλευρὰν αὐτοῦ, οὐ μὴ πιστεύσω.

verses.restored: After eight days his disciples were again inside, and Thomas with them. Jesus comes, the doors having been locked, and stood into the midst and said, Peace to you.

familiar.text: And after eight days again his disciples were within, and Thomas with them: then came Jesus, the doors being shut, and stood in the midst, and said, Peace be unto you.

modern.text: Eight days later, His disciples were once again inside with the doors locked, and Thomas was with them. Jesus came and stood among them and said, “Peace be with you.”

original.text: Καὶ μεθʼ ἡμέρας ὀκτὼ πάλιν ἦσαν ἔσω οἱ μαθηταὶ αὐτοῦ καὶ Θωμᾶς μετʼ αὐτῶν. ἔρχεται ὁ Ἰησοῦς τῶν θυρῶν κεκλεισμένων, καὶ ἔστη εἰς τὸ μέσον καὶ εἶπεν· Εἰρήνη ὑμῖν.

verses.restored: Then he says to Thomas, Bring your finger here and see my hands; bring your hand and put it into my side; and do not become untrusting but trusting.

familiar.text: Then saith he to Thomas, Reach hither thy finger, and behold my hands; and reach hither thy hand, and thrust it into my side: and be not faithless, but believing.

modern.text: Then Jesus said to Thomas, “Put your finger here and look at My hands. Reach out your hand and put it into My side. Stop doubting and believe.”

original.text: εἶτα λέγει τῷ Θωμᾷ· Φέρε τὸν δάκτυλόν σου ὧδε καὶ ἴδε τὰς χεῖράς μου, καὶ φέρε τὴν χεῖρά σου καὶ βάλε εἰς τὴν πλευράν μου, καὶ μὴ γίνου ἄπιστος ἀλλὰ πιστός.

verses.restored: Thomas answered and said to him, My Lord and my Divine.

familiar.text: And Thomas answered and said unto him, My LORD and my God.

modern.text: Thomas replied, “My Lord and my God!”

original.text: ⸀ἀπεκρίθη Θωμᾶς καὶ εἶπεν αὐτῷ· Ὁ κύριός μου καὶ ὁ θεός μου.

verses.restored: Jesus says to him, Because you have seen me, have you trusted? Blessed/flourishing are those not seeing and trusting.

familiar.text: Jesus saith unto him, Thomas, because thou hast seen me, thou hast believed: blessed are they that have not seen, and yet have believed.

modern.text: Jesus said to him, “Because you have seen Me, you have believed; blessed are those who have not seen and yet have believed.” The Purpose of John’s Book

original.text: λέγει αὐτῷ ὁ Ἰησοῦς· Ὅτι ἑώρακάς με πεπίστευκας; μακάριοι οἱ μὴ ἰδόντες καὶ πιστεύσαντες.

verses.restored: Therefore many other signs Jesus did before the disciples, which are not written in this scroll.

familiar.text: And many other signs truly did Jesus in the presence of his disciples, which are not written in this book:

modern.text: Jesus performed many other signs in the presence of His disciples, which are not written in this book.

original.text: Πολλὰ μὲν οὖν καὶ ἄλλα σημεῖα ἐποίησεν ὁ Ἰησοῦς ἐνώπιον τῶν ⸀μαθητῶν, ἃ οὐκ ἔστιν γεγραμμένα ἐν τῷ βιβλίῳ τούτῳ·

verses.restored: But these have been written so that you may trust that Jesus is the Messiah, the Son of the Divine, and that trusting you may have life in his name.

familiar.text: But these are written, that ye might believe that Jesus is the Christ, the Son of God; and that believing ye might have life through his name.

modern.text: But these are written so that you may believe that Jesus is the Christ, the Son of God, and that by believing you may have life in His name.

original.text: ταῦτα δὲ γέγραπται ἵνα ⸀πιστεύητε ὅτι Ἰησοῦς ἐστιν ὁ χριστὸς ὁ υἱὸς τοῦ θεοῦ, καὶ ἵνα πιστεύοντες ζωὴν ἔχητε ἐν τῷ ὀνόματι αὐτοῦ.
